name: preview-bar
title: Preview bar
description: Keeps build identity, expiry, feedback and relocking available after unlock. Does not verify codes, persist state, or grant or revoke access. Contract: the consumer owns lifecycle timestamps and action callbacks.

meta.whenToUse: After unlock, build identity, remaining lifetime, feedback and relock should stay reachable without covering the work.
meta.notFor: The locked state. Use a gate block for that; this is post-unlock chrome. For relock alone inside chrome you already have, use the Relock control.
pitfalls: `onRelock` only calls back. The bar hides nothing: set your own `unlocked` to false and move focus yourself.
Omitting `onRelock` omits the relock control rather than rendering an action that does nothing.
meta.contract: Keeps build identity, expiry, feedback and relocking available after unlock. Does not verify codes, persist state, or grant or revoke access. Contract: the consumer owns lifecycle timestamps and action callbacks.

props.name: expiresAt
props.description: ISO 8601 expiry timestamp with timezone. Displayed deterministically in UTC.

props.name: onRelock
props.description: Called when the consumer should relock the preview; required.

props.name: feedbackHref
props.description: Feedback destination. Takes precedence over callback; relative, http(s), or mailto.

props.name: onFeedback
props.description: Feedback callback when no destination URL is supplied.

props.name: labels
props.type: { navigation?: string; preview?: string; expires?: string; invalidExpiry?: string; feedback?: string; relock?: string; }

props.name: theme
props.description: Explicit theme; omitted follows the system preference.

meta.a11y: Native controls, visible focus, localized labels; lifecycle messages use polite announcements. No modal dialog is created.

docs: UI only. Read https://knock.codes/docs/preview-bar.md. Consumers own authorization.
